chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Jameela, from his grandfather Abi Jameela, from one of his companions, who said:
Had patience not been created before the affliction, the believer would have cracked apart, just as the egg cracks upon the rock.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of patience being created before affliction in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to highlight the ontological precedence of *sabr* (patience) as a divine attribute created before trials, ensuring believers possess the inherent capacity to endure hardship. The metaphor of an egg cracking on a smooth stone (*as-safa*) vividly illustrates the fragility of the human spirit when stripped of this spiritual fortitude, emphasizing that patience is not merely a reaction but a pre-existing divine gift. This aligns with Shia theological emphasis on *sabr* as a foundational virtue that preserves the believer's integrity amidst *bala'* (divine testing).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Jameela, from a grandfather of Abu Jameela, from one of his companions,
‘Heasws said: ‘Had the patience not been Created before the affliction, a ‘Momin’ (Believer), it would have torn the Momin into pieces just as the egg cracks upon the rock’.
en.sarwar: 20. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn abu Jamilah from his grad father abu Jamilah from certain individuals of his people from who have said: “The Imam said, ‘
Had patience not been created before misfortune, it would have torn the believer into pieces like an egg hit against a rock.’”
